members.name: AvailableFormats
members.description:
Retrieves a collection of available data formats that the DataObject contains.
### Syntax
`Function AvailableFormats() As DataObjectFormats`
### Return Value
This function returns a `DataObjectFormats` collection, an enumerable set of `DataObjectFormat` objects. Each `DataObjectFormat` object represents a format in which the data stored in the DataObject can be retrieved or set, providing properties like `FormatType` (indicating the format type as a `ClipboardConstants` value) and `Name` (a string representing the format name).
### Example
```vb
' Assume a DataObject has various data formats available
Dim myDataObject As New DataObject
Dim format As DataObjectFormat
' Retrieve the collection of available data formats
Dim availableFormats As DataObjectFormats
availableFormats = myDataObject.AvailableFormats()
' Iterate through the collection and display each format name and type
For Each format In availableFormats
    Debug.Print format.Name & "-" & format.FormatType
Next format
```
### Remarks
The `AvailableFormats` function is useful for determining what types of data are currently stored in a `DataObject`. This can be particularly helpful when working with clipboard operations or drag-and-drop features where the data formats of the incoming data are not known in advance.

members.name: Clear
members.description:
Clears all data from the DataObject.
### Syntax
`Sub Clear()`
### Example
```vb
' Create a new instance of a DataObject
Dim myDataObject As New DataObject
' Set some data on the DataObject
myDataObject.SetData "Some text"
' Clear the data from the DataObject
myDataObject.Clear
```
### Remarks
The `Clear` method removes all data formats and data from the DataObject. After calling `Clear`, 
the DataObject will no longer contain any data until new data is set with `SetData` or similar methods.
This is particularly useful when reusing a DataObject for multiple operations or ensuring that it does not hold onto 
any data past its intended use.

members.name: Files
members.description:
Retrieves a collection of file names from a DataObject that contains file data.
### Syntax
`Property Get Files() As Collection`
### Return Value
The property returns a `Collection` of strings, where each string is the fully qualified path of a file present in the DataObject.
### Example
```vb
' Assume a DataObject has been filled with file data via a drag-and-drop operation
Dim myDataObject As New DataObject
Dim file As Variant
' Retrieve the collection of file names
Dim files As Collection
Set files = myDataObject.Files
' Iterate through the collection and display each file name
For Each file In files
    Debug.Print file
Next file
```
### Remarks
The `Files` property is commonly used when handling drag-and-drop file operations in a user interface. It allows the application to retrieve the list of files that have been dragged into it. This property is read-only, and attempting to set it will result in a compile-time error.

members.name: GetData
members.signature: Function GetData([TypeHint(ClipboardConstants)] ByVal sFormat As Integer) As Variant
members.description:
Retrieves data stored in the DataObject in a specified format.
### Syntax
`Function GetData(Optional ByVal Format As Variant) As Variant`
### Parameters
`Format` (Optional): The format in which to retrieve the data. Can be a standard Clipboard format or a custom format.
### Return Value
The method returns the data in the DataObject as a Variant, in the specified format. If the format is not available, returns Nothing.
### Example
```vb
' Create a new instance of a DataObject
Dim myDataObject As New DataObject
' Set some text data on the DataObject
myDataObject.SetData "Some text", vbCFText
' Retrieve the data as text
Dim strData As String
strData = myDataObject.GetData(vbCFText)
If strData Is Nothing Then
    MsgBox "Data not available in the requested format"
Else
    MsgBox "Data retrieved: " & strData
End If
```
### Remarks
The `GetData` method is used to retrieve data from the DataObject that has been stored using the `SetData` method. 
If `Format` is omitted, the DataObject will attempt to retrieve the data in the format it was last set, 
or in a format that the DataObject deems the most appropriate based on the data types available.
This method is essential for transferring data between applications or components via the clipboard or drag-and-drop operations.

members.name: GetDataByName
members.signature: Function GetDataByName(ByVal Format As String) As Variant
members.description:
Retrieves data from a DataObject in the format specified by the format name.
### Syntax
`Function GetDataByName(ByVal Format As String) As Variant`
### Parameters
- **Format**: A `String` specifying the name of the format of the data to retrieve.
### Return Value
Returns the data contained in the DataObject that matches the specified format name. The data is returned as a `Variant`.
### Example
```vb
' Assume a DataObject contains data in the 'Text' format
Dim myDataObject As New DataObject
Dim theData As Variant
' Retrieve data in the 'Text' format
theData = myDataObject.GetDataByName("Text")
If Not IsEmpty(theData) Then
    MsgBox "Data in 'Text' format: " & theData
Else
    MsgBox "No data in 'Text' format was found." 
End If
```
### Remarks
The `GetDataByName` function is particularly useful for accessing data in a specific format from a `DataObject` when the format name is known but the numerical clipboard format value is not. This is common when working with data copied to the clipboard from other applications or during drag-and-drop operations.

members.name: GetFormat
members.signature: Function GetFormat([TypeHint(ClipboardConstants)] ByVal sFormat As Integer) As Boolean
members.description:
Checks if data stored in the DataObject is available in a specified format.
### Syntax
`Function GetFormat(Optional ByVal Format As Variant) As Boolean`
### Parameters
`Format` (Optional): The format to check for data availability. Can be a standard Clipboard format or a custom format.
### Return Value
The method returns `True` if data is available in the specified format; otherwise, it returns `False`.
### Example
```vb
' Create a new instance of a DataObject
Dim myDataObject As New DataObject
' Set some text data on the DataObject
myDataObject.SetData "Some text", vbCFText
' Check if the data is available in text format
If myDataObject.GetFormat(vbCFText) Then
    MsgBox "Data is available in the text format"
Else
    MsgBox "Data is not available in the requested format"
End If
```
### Remarks
The `GetFormat` method is used to check whether data in the DataObject is available in a specific format 
before attempting to retrieve it using the `GetData` method. This can prevent errors or unexpected results when 
working with data in various formats.

members.name: GetFormatByName
members.signature: Function GetFormatByName(ByVal Format As String) As Boolean
members.description:
Determines if a data object contains data in the specified format.
### Syntax
`Function GetFormatByName(ByVal Format As String) As Boolean`
### Parameters
- **Format**: A `String` specifying the name of the format to check for.
### Return Value
Returns `True` if the DataObject contains data in the format specified by `Format`. Otherwise, it returns `False`.
### Example
```vb
' Assume a DataObject might contain data in the 'Text' format
Dim myDataObject As New DataObject
' Check if 'Text' format data is available
If myDataObject.GetFormatByName("Text") Then
    MsgBox "Text format is available." 
Else
    MsgBox "Text format is not available." 
End If
```
### Remarks
The `GetFormatByName` function is useful when you need to check for the presence of data in a specific format within a `DataObject`, especially when interacting with the clipboard or during drag-and-drop operations where the data may come in various formats.

members.name: SetData
members.signature: Sub SetData(Optional ByVal Value As Variant, [TypeHint(ClipboardConstants)] Optional ByVal Format As Variant)
members.description:
Assigns data to the DataObject with an optional specified format.
### Syntax
`Sub SetData(Value, [Format]`
### Parameters
`Value` - The data to set on the DataObject. The type can be anything that is storable in a Variant.
`Format` - [Optional] The format in which the data should be stored. This can be specified as a `ClipboardConstants` enumeration value.
### Example
```vb
' Create a new instance of a DataObject
Dim myDataObject As New DataObject
' Set text data on the DataObject without specifying the format
myDataObject.SetData "Hello, world!"
' Set data with a specified format
myDataObject.SetData someData, ClipboardConstants.CF_TEXT
```
### Remarks
The `SetData` method is used to add data to the DataObject. If the format is not specified, 
the DataObject may choose the default format based on the type of the `Value` provided. 
Specifying the `Format` allows the data to be stored and retrieved in a specific clipboard format.
When using custom data formats, ensure they are registered with the clipboard if necessary.

members.name: FormatType
members.description:
Allows get or set operations on the format type of the data within the DataObject.
### Syntax
' To retrieve the format type:
`Property Get FormatType() As ClipboardConstants`
' To assign a new format type:
`Property Let FormatType(ByVal newFormatType As ClipboardConstants)`
### Property Value
`ClipboardConstants` enumeration representing the clipboard format type of the data.
### Example
```vb
' Assume 'dataFormat' is a previously initialized DataObjectFormat object.
Dim fmtType As ClipboardConstants
fmtType = dataFormat.FormatType
' Check the current format type
If fmtType = ClipboardConstants.vbCFText Then
    MsgBox "Current format is text."
Else
    ' Set the format type to text
    dataFormat.FormatType = ClipboardConstants.vbCFText
    MsgBox "Format type set to text."
End If
```
### Remarks
The `FormatType` property allows you to get or set the type of data that is contained within a `DataObject`. The value returned or set corresponds to one of the constants in the `ClipboardConstants` enumeration, such as `vbCFText` or `vbCFBitmap`.

members.name: ReadProperty
members.signature: Function ReadProperty(ByVal Name As String, Optional ByVal DefaultValue As Variant) As Variant
members.description:
Reads a property value from a PropertyBag object.
### Syntax
`Function ReadProperty(ByVal Name As String, Optional ByVal DefaultValue As Variant) As Variant`
### Parameters
- `Name`: The name of the property to read.
- `DefaultValue`: An optional parameter that specifies the return value if the property is not found. The data type can be any.
### Return Value
The function returns the value of the specified property. If the property is not found, it returns the `DefaultValue` if provided; otherwise, it returns `Null`.
### Example
```vb
' Assume 'propBag' is a previously initialized PropertyBag object with properties set.
Dim myValue As Variant
myValue = propBag.ReadProperty("MyProperty", "DefaultValue")
```
### Remarks
The `ReadProperty` function is typically used when an object needs to read its state from a PropertyBag, such as during the `ReadProperties` event when implementing persistence in ActiveX controls (UserControls) or documents.

members.name: WriteProperty
members.signature: Sub WriteProperty(ByVal Name As String, ByVal Value As Variant, Optional ByVal DefaultValue As Variant)
members.description:
Writes a property value to a PropertyBag object.
### Syntax
`Sub WriteProperty(ByVal Name As String, ByVal Value As Variant, Optional ByVal DefaultValue As Variant)`
### Parameters
- `Name`: The name of the property to write.
- `Value`: The value to write to the property. The data type can be any that is supported by the PropertyBag.
- `DefaultValue`: An optional parameter that specifies the value the client should assume as default when reading the property.
### Return Value
None. This is a Sub procedure and does not return a value.
### Example
```vb
' Assume 'propBag' is a previously initialized PropertyBag object.
propBag.WriteProperty("MyProperty", "SomeValue", "DefaultValue")
```
### Remarks
The `WriteProperty` procedure is typically used when an object needs to save its state to a PropertyBag, such as during the `WriteProperties` event when implementing persistence in ActiveX controls or documents. The `DefaultValue` parameter is used to optimize storage by not storing the value if it is the same as the default.

members.name: Contents
members.description:
Retrieves or sets the entire state of the contents of a PropertyBag object.
### Syntax
`Property Let Contents(ByVal NewValue As Variant)`
`Property Get Contents() As Variant`
### Parameters
- `NewValue`: The new value to assign to the contents of the PropertyBag when using `Let`.
### Property Value
A Variant containing the entire state of the PropertyBag when using `Get`.  The Variant subtype is a byte-array.
### Example
```vb
' Assume 'propBag' is a previously initialized PropertyBag object.
' To retrieve the contents:
Dim bagContents As Variant
bagContents = propBag.Contents

' To set the contents:
' Assume 'newContents' is a Variant containing the state to load into the PropertyBag
propBag.Contents = newContents
```
### Remarks
The `Contents` property is used to retrieve or set the complete state of the PropertyBag. This is useful when you need to load or save the state of the PropertyBag in one operation. When setting the `Contents`, the existing state is replaced by the `NewValue`. When reading the `Contents`, the entire state is retrieved as a Variant, which can then be manipulated as needed.
